adaptations.withheld: sacred or restricted dance: no teaching adaptations

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: The right hand holds and manipulates the metal scissors, striking them in rhythm.
movement_profile.footwork: Includes walking on the tips of the toes and complex zapateo (foot-tapping) patterns.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Competitive duel format; dancers perform in turns.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Includes acrobatic jumps and balancing acts, sometimes performed on church towers.
movement_profile.posture: Upright and athletic, often involving balancing on one foot.

signature_moves.description: A competitive duel where dancers challenge each other to perform increasingly difficult physical feats.
signature_moves.name: Atipanakuy

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Increases in intensity as the competition progresses.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Do not enter a church while wearing the performance costume.

music_profile.musical_form: Music varies by the stage of the dance, such as 'Pasacalle' for street processions.
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Rhythmic clashing of metal plates synchronized with harp and violin melodies.
music_profile.sound_description: The sound is defined by the melodic interplay of a harp and violin, punctuated by the sharp, rhythmic metallic clashing of the scissors.

basic_steps: Marcha: Walking on the tips of the toes to greet the audience.
Zapateo: Rhythmic footwork performed during festivities.
Acrobatic feats: High-level physical challenges including balancing and jumping.
teaching.formation: Competitive duel between two or more dancers, each with their own musician.
teaching.level_notes: The dance is highly advanced, requiring years of training starting from childhood.
teaching.rhythm: Rhythmic striking of metal plates in time with harp and violin music.
